title: New album, new books and finding a label
summary: The album's new charts are meant to attract a label; he cites a note from Bruce Lundvall that it should be his biggest album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, sure, because -- in other words, why we're all working so hard, at least, I am, and I've tried so very hard with this particular album, is to prove this sort of thing, plus the fact that the only way I'm going to get a major -- or any sensible label that is willing to put up the money without a fight that's necessary just to get the album to where it should be normally, is by coming up with new and different books.
Some people have a broader aspect, they have more courage in some direction, or maybe they've had more time. But whatever it is, I've got a couple of scratched-out lines from

Bruce Lundfall on the back of Peter Levinson's note, which says, "I thought the album was great, it should be Woody's biggest album. I guess Woody's still younger than all of us. Signed, Bruce." So that doesn't mean he's interested in recording my band, but he is aware, he knows what I'm into and so on, and my whole -- most important thing right now is to make this album important enough so I can get with a label who's willing to --
To what I need, because of where I am.
